messages:
Elena: Hey team — customer ACME-Tenant reported their monthly credits showed 0 an hour before their expected reset. They hit 429s from our API and UI showed zero until it suddenly refilled at UTC midnight. Asking for quick triage steps. tenant_id: tn_acme_42, observed around 2026-03-15T22:12:00-07:00.

Elena: Repro notes from the customer: long-running streaming session + a batch job that generated embeddings. They saw a steady token burn, then UI jumped to 0 while API returned 429 with body: `{"error":"quota_exhausted","code":429}` and headers: `X-Request-Id: req_9f3a`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-Tenant-TZ: America/Los_Angeles`.

OncallBot: Alert: tenant tn_acme_42 credit pool dropped to 0 at 2026-03-15T22:11:47Z (spike consumption). Related incidents: none.

Sanjay: Thanks Elena — can you paste the request_id from the 429s and one example of the raw usage log (tenant, timestamp, tokens charged)? Also did they have any reserved/dedicated capacity or were they on hosted?

Elena: Request id from API: req_9f3a and another req_9f3b. Usage log sample: `tn_acme_42 | 2026-03-15T21:58:10Z | streaming_session | tokens=120k` and `tn_acme_42 | 2026-03-15T22:05:33Z | embeddings_batch | tokens=95k`. They are on hosted with burst credits (no Dedicated). Customer claims monthly bucket should reset at midnight PST, but we document UTC midnight.

Maya: Quick billing note: Core refill job is UTC midnight (00:00:00Z) for all tenants. We do have a UI cache that shows tenant-local tz times sometimes and a separate background job that repopulates the visible bucket; in rare race conditions the UI can flip to 0 before the refill job finishes.

Sanjay: Two hypotheses: (1) Actual exhaustion — combined streaming + batch consumed full monthly bucket earlier than expected (tokens add up). (2) Display/invalidation race — UI cache TTL and a delayed cache refresh made it look like zero earlier even though backend had scheduled refill at UTC midnight. We should confirm actual ledger state around the timestamps. Can you attach ledger snapshot for tn_acme_42 21:50-22:20Z?

Elena: Pasted ledger excerpt from internal audit: `tn_acme_42 | ledger_balance_before=230k | charged=215k | ledger_balance_after=15k` then two big inflight charges at 22:05 and 22:11 consumed remaining 15k. Then at 23:59:59Z refill job added 1,000,000 tokens. So looks like real exhaustion + then refill. Customer timezone confusion added noise.

Maya: That matches. FYI the UI shows tenant-local reset time if tenant has profile timezone set; however the authoritative refill is UTC. We'll send a short FAQ update.

Sanjay: Root cause = actual quota exhaustion due to combined high-consumption streaming + embeddings batch late in billing day. Secondary contributor = tenant expected local-midnight reset which differs from our UTC policy. Action items: 1) Elena — share ledger & request ids to customer and explain UTC reset + provide tokens/time of refill (done). 2) Maya — flag billing docs + add note about streaming cumulative counts. 3) Ops/Infra follow-up: consider lowering UI cache TTL for quota display or show authoritative server-time next to visible bucket.

Elena: Customer replied, OK with explanation but wants suggestions to avoid repeat. Suggested mitigations: enforce streaming per-connection throttles, move heavy embeddings to next day, or purchase Dedicated/Reserved capacity to avoid burst depletion.

Sanjay: Also recommend we add a short API header `X-Quota-Next-Reset: 2026-03-16T00:00:00Z` for visibility and a `X-Quota-Visible-TZ` so UIs can show authoritative times. Filing infra ticket.

Maya: I'll draft a customer-facing note and billing doc update. Elena, can you close the support ticket once the customer accepts the mitigation options? :thumbsup:

Elena: Yep will close after confirmation. Closing notes to customer include ledger excerpt, UTC reset policy, and mitigation options.

OncallBot: Incident closed (no platform bug).
